FINAL / 4 - ADD HIGH-RES VIEWS TO AN EXISTING SPLAT DATASET

Takes the SAME panorama your dataset was built from, renders full-resolution pinhole views of it, and registers them INTO that dataset's existing SphereSfM reconstruction. The COLMAP camera information is regenerated over the combination of both -- the WAN fly-through frames AND the hires renders -- in one sparse model.

WHY THIS IS WORTH DOING: the cube faces SphereSfM produces are 360x360. That is the ceiling on how sharp your splat can get, no matter how you train it. These hires views go in at 1920x1080 (or 4K) of real panorama detail, from the same scene, with real SfM-solved poses.

HOW IT WORKS (no pose transfer, no scale fitting, no trust required):
COLMAP holds a MIXED model. The WAN panoramas stay SPHERE cameras; the hires renders enter as their own PINHOLE camera, matched against the existing frames by real image features, and bundle-adjusted in the SAME reconstruction. Their poses come out of the same solve as everything else. The existing cameras are FIXED during registration (adjust_existing_cameras=false), so the add is purely additive: it cannot move poses that already train well. Verified on 040_CafeLounge: 24/24 views registered, ~0.8px residuals, 0 existing poses moved, points3D 24530 -> 25926.

REQUIREMENTS:
  * dataset_dir = a SphereSfM dataset root (holds images/, sparse/, _spheresfm_work/). It MUST have been built with mode=colmap_now -- the add registers against the original spherical reconstruction, which panorama_only datasets do not have.
  * The panorama here MUST be the one the dataset was built from. SfM matches the renders against the existing frames by image content; views of another scene simply fail to register (the node says so rather than writing garbage).
  * Keep movement_scale modest and edge_mode=stretch. Registration matches REAL detail -- pixels invented by a hole fill match nothing.

AFTER IT RUNS: train exactly as before, same command, same folder. The hires views are just extra images in images/ with poses in sparse/0.
  LichtFeld-Studio.exe -d <dataset_dir> -o <out> --headless --train --strategy mcmc --max-cap 2000000 --sh-degree 2

THE ADD IS DESTRUCTIVE to the dataset folder (it rewrites sparse/0 and drops new images into images/). It is designed to be safe -- existing poses are pinned and existing faces are left alone -- but if you want to keep a pristine copy, copy the dataset folder first.

Running it TWICE just adds more views (hires_ numbering continues); it does not duplicate.

If views fail to register, the node tells you instead of writing a broken dataset. Fixes, in order:
  1. lower movement_scale (renders stay closer to what the pano really shows)
  2. edge_mode=stretch (no invented pixels)
  3. raise max_num_features
  4. lower abs_pose_min_num_inliers

match_stride: raise to 2-3 if your base dataset has many hundreds of frames and matching is slow. Neighbouring pano frames are near-duplicates, so every 2nd still ties the views in.
